title: Freya and the Hollow
premise: Juniper Vane, a cartographer who once mapped the unmapped realms, has hidden for seven years in the city of Corvane, selling harmless charms while magic is outlawed by the Hollow King. When the old gods begin answering prayers again, Juniper's charms start working—and drawing attention—forcing them to flee into the wilds with a disgraced inquisitor, Sera, and a god-touched child named Wren. They discover the king was hollowed out years ago and replaced by a devouring entity that feeds on memory, erasing magic and history alike; unbinding him means restoring what was stolen, including Juniper's own deliberately forgotten past as the cartographer who first opened the door for it. In the end, Juniper chooses to remember everything at terrible cost, uses their maps of memory to trap the entity inside its own hunger, frees the broken king to face justice outside the law, and accepts exile rather than power, leaving Corvane's fate to its people.
about_author: P. M. Crane is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing half-burned municipal records before turning to fiction full-time. They live near the coast with two opinionated cats and an ever-growing collection of antique maps.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Debt
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Seven years after burning their own maps, they sell quiet charms in Corvane's night market, keeping their head down under the Hollow King's edicts. A desperate mother buys one for her sick daughter—and it works. Juniper feels the old power stir and knows invisibility just ended. Beat: dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Across the city, prayers are being answered: wells refill, dead gardens bloom. The old gods are waking, and every answered prayer points back to Juniper's charm. Inquisitors sweep the market. Juniper packs their satchel of instruments and prepares to run. Beat: hunted calm.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor Who Knocks
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera Ilvane, once the crown's finest inquisitor, now demoted for asking too many questions about the king's strange decrees, is ordered to find the charm-seller. She recognizes the work instantly—it matches evidence from a case she was forbidden to close. Beat: conflicted duty.

chapters.title: Ash and Alleyways
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Cornered in the alleys, Juniper expects arrest—but Sera lets them go, demanding answers about the closed case instead. Before either can decide, Wren, a feral god-touched child, appears speaking in the old gods' voices, naming Juniper 'door-maker.' Beat: reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: What the Child Remembers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Through Wren's fragmented, luminous memories we see the gods' return: something ate their temples, their names, their worshippers. Wren leads Juniper and Sera through a hidden gate out of Corvane while inquisitors burn the night market behind them. Beat: grief and flight.

chapters.title: Roads Not on Any Map
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. In the wilds, Juniper's suppressed gift resurfaces—they can read the land's memory, seeing roads that were erased. Each vision costs them pieces of their own past, which they've been trading away for years without admitting why. Beat: mounting self-dread.

chapters.title: The Village That Forgot Its Name
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The trio finds a village where no one remembers anything older than seven years—the exact span of the Hollow King's reign. An elder clutches a blank stone tablet that should hold their founding story. Sera realizes the king isn't enforcing forgetting; he's consuming it. Beat: cold revelation.

chapters.title: Sera's Heresy
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Flashbacks interleave with the present as Sera recalls the case she couldn't close: a palace servant found hollow-eyed, babbling about 'the thing wearing his crown.' Her superiors buried it. Now she understands she wasn't demoted—she was silenced. Beat: faith breaking open.

chapters.title: The God Beneath the Hill
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Following Wren's voices, they reach a hill-shrine where a diminished god, barely more than a voice, confirms it: the Hollow King devours memory to feed itself, and only the one who opened its door can close it again. Juniper denies knowing how. Beat: denial cracking.

chapters.title: Seven Years Ago
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The shrine forces a partial return of Juniper's traded memories: they were the realm's greatest cartographer, hired by the young king to map the spaces between worlds—and they drew the passage that let the entity in. They fled and burned their work. Beat: guilt made flesh.

chapters.title: Wren Is Taken
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Crown riders ambush the group; Wren, whose god-voices the entity craves, is captured. Juniper could escape but turns back, using a dangerous memory-map to follow the riders. Sera chooses them over her oath openly now. Beat: sacrifice chosen.

chapters.title: Into the Pale City
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Disguised as pilgrims, they enter Corvane, greyer than Juniper remembered—literally; color drains wherever the king's influence thickens. They find allies among the charm-buyers Juniper helped over the years, an underground network of small mercies. Beat: fragile hope.

chapters.title: The King's Empty Eyes
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Using her old credentials, Sera gets audience and sees the king up close: his eyes reflect nothing, his speeches loop phrases from decades past. He is a puppet of meat and ritual. She escapes the palace knowing there is nothing left to save but the body. Beat: horror clarified.

chapters.title: The Price of Remembering
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. To unbind the king, Juniper must recover every memory they sold or burned—including the full map of the door. The remaining gods offer restoration, but warn: total recall will also return the person Juniper was, whom they may not be able to live with. Beat: choice weighted.

chapters.title: The Vault of Sold Things
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Deep beneath the city, in a vault where confiscated magic is stored, Juniper reclaims their memories piece by piece, reliving betrayals and arrogance as the old Juniper reassembles. Sera anchors them, and Wren's returned presence steadies the gods' chorus. Beat: painful integration.

chapters.title: Crown of Hunger
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV (the entity). Inside the king, the Hollow Thing senses the door-maker's return and offers Juniper a bargain: restore your erased life, rule beside it, forget guilt forever. It shows Juniper seductive visions of a world with no painful pasts. Beat: temptation at full strength.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper refuses—not with heroics but with a cartographer's truth: a world without memory is a world without roads, and roads are how people find each other. The entity drops pretense and moves to consume the city's remaining memories at once. Beat: defiance before catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Juniper, Sera, and Wren assault the throne room during the entity's great feeding. Juniper redraws the original map in reverse, Wren channels the gods' returning names, and Sera holds the hollowed king's body steady as the entity is pulled toward the closing door. Beat: climax, all threads converging.

chapters.title: Inside the Door
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The map traps the entity not by destroying it but by giving it infinite hunger with nothing left to eat but itself—a labyrinth drawn from its own consumed memories. Juniper nearly follows it in, lured by the promise of forgetting again; Sera's voice pulls them back. Beat: darkest moment survived.

chapters.title: A King on Trial
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The freed king, a broken man guilty of opening the door willingly, faces the citizens he wronged—not a royal court but a public reckoning Sera insists upon, justice outside the law's machinery. Some want mercy, some blood; the city argues its way toward something new. Beat: justice as process.

chapters.title: Maps for the Living
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Magic is legal again, but Juniper declines any position of power, instead teaching ordinary people to read the land's memory themselves. Wren, adopted by the recovering village, begins mapping the gods' returning shrines. Beat: bittersweet renewal.

chapters.title: The Road Out
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Unable to stay where their old self did harm, Juniper walks out of Corvane at dawn with fresh paper and empty pages, Sera choosing exile beside them. Ahead lie realms still unmapped—and this time, Juniper intends to draw them honestly. Beat: earned departure, open horizon.
